text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Pakistan bought 180,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat and 90,000 tonnes of Australian wheat over the weekend, several U.S. exporters said. The delivery dates were slated for January 8 to 31.

WHEAT TENDER - Bangladesh has tendered for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. grade-2 or Australian Standard or better Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21, food ministry officials said on Sunday. The ministry would open the tender on January 18. The result of the bidding will be known within two to three days after opening of the tender.

WHEAT TENDER - Yemen has postponed until January 7 soft wheat grain and soft wheat flour tenders initially scheduled for December 26, European grain traders said on Monday. Yemen is seeking 200,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat flour for shipment between February and June and 200,000 tonnes of new crop U.S. or Canadian or Australian soft white wheat for July-September shipment, they said.
WHEAT TENDER - Sri Lanka may seek in early January 100,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for late January shipment, U.S. exporters said.

WHEAT AND BARLEY TENDER - Tunisia launched a tender for Tuesday for the purchase of four lots of barley of 25,000 tonnes each and two lots of soft wheat of 25,000 tonnes each, traders said on Saturday.

SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The Commodity Credit Corp of the U.S. Agriculture Department said it will tender for 10,370 tonnes of U.S. bulk crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. The delivery period was slated for February 3-18. Offers were requested by January 7. Successful offerers will be notified on January 8.
RICE TENDER - The Japanese Food Agency will hold an import tender for 7,000 tonnes of rice on December 25, agency officials said on Friday.

MARKET TALK - The grains and oilseeds business from Japan to the Philippines will probably slip into a coma this week as people take off for a long Christmas holiday, regional traders said on Monday. Only a sharp drop in grains and oilseeds futures prices in the United States could induce some buyers to wake up and come in for some bargain-hunting, although the prospect looked dim, traders said.
